\chapter{Rickshaw and Horse: One New Consonant}
\label{ch:mw-transport-five}
\hlchaptermodality{22}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can add rickshaw and horse to the transport map after learning only \mw{श} and reusing the dotted consonant from clothes.}

Two more source-attested transport words begin by ear, add only \mw{श}, and join the earlier three in a non-compensatory four-skill payoff.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[rikśā]{Hear \emph{rikśā} — rickshaw}

\label{lesson:MW-C17-hear-riksha}



\begin{quote}
Recall the three-word transport payoff, say wife, then write goods.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{What to know first}
\begin{quote}
\emph{rikśā} — \textbf{rickshaw}
\end{quote}

Hear the three beats, point to a rickshaw picture, and say the word once. Keep the written cluster covered for now.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://www.marwaripathshala.com/marwari-lesson-10-english}{Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 10}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[śa]{\mw{श} — the \emph{sh} in rickshaw}

\label{lesson:MW-W17-sha}



\begin{quote}
Recall the five-word shopping payoff, say rickshaw, then write wife and familiar \textbf{\mw{स}}.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Script — one sign}
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\mw{श}} — \emph{sha}
\end{quote}

Notice the vertical stem and the looped left side. Keep it distinct from familiar \textbf{\mw{स}}.

\subsection*{Your turn}
Trace \textbf{\mw{श}} once. Copy it once. Cover it, wait five seconds, and write it from the \emph{sh} sound cue.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://www.unicode.org/charts/PDF/U0900.pdf}{Unicode Devanagari chart}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[rikśā]{\mw{रिक्शा} — rickshaw on the page}

\label{lesson:MW-C17-riksha}



\begin{quote}
Say rickshaw and child, then write \textbf{\mw{श}} and \textbf{\mw{्}}.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{What to know first}
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\mw{रि}} + \textbf{\mw{क्}} + \textbf{\mw{शा}} $\to$ \textbf{\mw{रिक्शा}} — \emph{rikśā} — rickshaw
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Look, cover, wait five seconds, and write \textbf{\mw{रिक्शा}}. Check that \textbf{\mw{ि}} appears before \textbf{\mw{र}} but is read after it, and that \textbf{\mw{्}} joins \textbf{\mw{क}} to \textbf{\mw{श}}.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://www.marwaripathshala.com/marwari-lesson-10-english}{Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 10}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[ghoṛo]{Hear \emph{ghoṛo} — horse}

\label{lesson:MW-C17-hear-ghodo}



\begin{quote}
Say rickshaw, vehicle, and clothes, then write \textbf{\mw{च}} and \textbf{\mw{ड़}}.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{What to know first}
\begin{quote}
\emph{ghoṛo} — \textbf{horse}
\end{quote}

Hear the breathy first sound and curled middle sound. Point to a horse and say the word once.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://www.marwaripathshala.com/marwari-lesson-10-english}{Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 10}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[ghoṛo]{\mw{घोड़ो} — horse on the page}

\label{lesson:MW-C17-ghodo}



\begin{quote}
Say horse, then write vehicle and child.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{What to know first}
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\mw{घो}} + \textbf{\mw{ड़ो}} $\to$ \textbf{\mw{घोड़ो}} — \emph{ghoṛo} — horse
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Look, cover, wait five seconds, and write \textbf{\mw{घोड़ो}}. Check both long-o marks and the dot below \textbf{\mw{ड}}.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://www.marwaripathshala.com/marwari-lesson-10-english}{Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 10}.
\end{tcolorbox}

\section[Practice]{Payoff — five transport words in four skills}

\label{lesson:MW-C17-transport-five}



\begin{quote}
Recall the earlier three-word transport payoff and the twelve-label family payoff, then say expensive.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
1. Identify five heard words. 2. Produce five words from meaning cues. 3. Match five printed cards to meanings. 4. Write all five heard words without a model.

Pass each skill separately. This vocabulary foundation does not yet claim a ticket purchase, timetable question, or problem report.

\section[Practice]{Close the writing loop for \mw{ड़} and \mw{श}}

\label{lesson:MW-R17-script-close}



\begin{quote}
Recall the five-word transport payoff, then write expensive.
\end{quote}
